title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What is a Map?
text:
What is a Map?

Key terms: map, representation, symbols

A map is a representation of an area, showing its features and how to navigate it. It's like a treasure guide that helps us find our way. Maps can be physical, political, or thematic, and they use symbols, distance, and direction to convey information.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is a Map? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Cardinal Directions
text:
Cardinal Directions

Key terms: cardinal directions, north, south

Cardinal directions are the main directions on a map: north, south, east, and west. They help us understand the layout of a place and how to navigate it. We can also use intermediate directions like northeast, southeast, and so on.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Cardinal Directions in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Map Scale
text:
Map Scale

Key terms: map scale, distance, measurement

A map scale is a way to show the relationship between the size of a feature on the map and its actual size in the real world. It helps us understand how to measure distances and navigate the map.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Map Scale in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Map Symbols
text:
Map Symbols

Key terms: map symbols, representation, features

Map symbols are small drawings or marks that represent features on the map, like buildings, roads, or natural elements. They help us understand the map and navigate it more easily.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Map Symbols in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Locating Places on a Map
text:
Locating Places on a Map

Key terms: locating places, map features, navigation

Locating places on a map involves using the map's features, like cardinal directions and symbols, to understand where things are and how to get to them. It's an important skill for navigation and understanding the world around us.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Locating Places on a Map in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Understanding Maps
text:
Understanding Maps

Key terms: understanding maps, map types, information

Understanding maps involves recognizing the different types of maps, like physical, political, and thematic, and how they use symbols, distance, and direction to convey information. It's an important skill for navigating the world and making informed decisions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Understanding Maps in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Representing the Earth
text:
Representing the Earth

Key terms: globe, coordinates

The Earth is a sphere, but it's difficult to represent it accurately on a flat map. A globe is a better representation of the Earth's geography because it's also a sphere. We can use a system of coordinates to locate places on the globe.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Representing the Earth in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Latitude and Longitude
text:
Latitude and Longitude

Key terms: latitude, longitude, Prime Meridian

Latitude measures the distance from the Equator, while longitude measures the distance from the Prime Meridian. We can use these two coordinates to locate any place on the Earth. Latitude and longitude are measured in degrees, with the Equator at 0° and the poles at 90°.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Latitude and Longitude in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Time Zones
text:
Time Zones

Key terms: time zones, standard time, meridian

Time zones are areas on the Earth that follow the same standard time. We can calculate the local time of a place by measuring its longitude. Most countries adopt a standard time based on a meridian passing through them.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Time Zones in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | International Date Line
text:
International Date Line

Key terms: International Date Line, date line

The International Date Line is an imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole, approximately at 180° longitude. Crossing this line changes the date by one day. It's used to divide the world into two days.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to International Date Line in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Grid of Latitudes and Longitudes
text:
Grid of Latitudes and Longitudes

Key terms: grid, latitudes, longitudes

A grid of latitudes and longitudes is a system of imaginary lines that run from east to west (parallel to the Equator) and north to south (from pole to pole) respectively. This grid helps us to precisely define the location of any place on the Earth.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Grid of Latitudes and Longitudes in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Prime Meridian
text:
Prime Meridian

Key terms: Prime Meridian, Greenwich Meridian

The Prime Meridian is an imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole, passing through Greenwich, England. It's used as a reference point to measure longitude and define the time zones.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Prime Meridian in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Measuring Longitude
text:
Measuring Longitude

Key terms: longitude, Prime Meridian, degrees

Longitude is measured by calculating the distance from the Prime Meridian. We can use this measurement to determine the local time of a place. Longitude is measured in degrees, with the Prime Meridian at 0° and the opposite line at 180°.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Measuring Longitude in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Understanding Time Zones
text:
Understanding Time Zones

Key terms: time zones, standard time, meridian

Time zones are areas on the Earth that follow the same standard time. We can calculate the local time of a place by measuring its longitude. Most countries adopt a standard time based on a meridian passing through them.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Understanding Time Zones in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What is Longitude?
text:
What is Longitude?

Key terms: longitude, time zones

Longitude is an imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole. It helps us measure the distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Longitude also marks the time and defines the time zones.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is Longitude? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | International Date Line
text:
International Date Line

Key terms: date line, 180 degrees

The International Date Line is an imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole, at 180 degrees longitude. Crossing the International Date Line changes the date by one day.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to International Date Line in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Time Zones
text:
Time Zones

Key terms: time zones, longitude

Time zones are areas on Earth that follow the same time. They are determined by the longitude of a place. When it's a certain time in one time zone, it's a different time in another time zone.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Time Zones in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Local Time vs Standard Time
text:
Local Time vs Standard Time

Key terms: local time, standard time

Local time is the time in a specific place, while standard time is the time in a region or country. Local time and standard time can be different, especially when crossing time zones.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Local Time vs Standard Time in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Latitude and Longitude
text:
Latitude and Longitude

Key terms: latitude, longitude

Latitude and longitude are two imaginary lines that help us locate a place on Earth. Latitude measures the distance north or south of the Equator, while longitude measures the distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Latitude and Longitude in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Equator and Prime Meridian
text:
Equator and Prime Meridian

Key terms: equator, prime meridian

The Equator is an imaginary line that runs around the middle of the Earth, at 0 degrees latitude. The Prime Meridian is an imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole, at 0 degrees longitude. They are used as references to measure latitude and longitude.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Equator and Prime Meridian in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Map Scales
text:
Map Scales

Key terms: map scale, ratio

A map scale is a ratio that shows the relationship between the size of a map and the size of the real-world place it represents. It helps us measure distances and understand the layout of a place.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Map Scales in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What are Oceans and Continents?
text:
What are Oceans and Continents?

Key terms: oceans, continents

Oceans and continents are large bodies of water and land on Earth. Oceans cover most of the planet's surface, while continents are large landmasses. They play a vital role in shaping the climate and supporting life on Earth.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What are Oceans and Continents? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Distribution of Water and Land
text:
Distribution of Water and Land

Key terms: hemispheres, ocean distribution

Oceans and continents are not distributed equally between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern Hemisphere, and the Pacific Ocean is the largest of all the oceans.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Distribution of Water and Land in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Ocean Life and Importance
text:
Ocean Life and Importance

Key terms: ocean life, oxygen production

Oceans are home to a vast array of plant and animal life, including coral reefs, fish, and whales. They play a crucial role in regulating the climate and producing oxygen, making them essential for life on Earth.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ocean Life and Importance in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Continents and Island Counting
text:
Continents and Island Counting

Key terms: continents, islands

Continents can be counted in different ways, with the most common count being seven. Islands are smaller pieces of land surrounded by water, and there are many islands around the world, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Continents and Island Counting in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Impact of Oceans on Human Life
text:
Impact of Oceans on Human Life

Key terms: ocean impact, human activity

Oceans have had a significant impact on human life, including providing food, trade routes, and cultural inspiration. However, human activities such as pollution and overfishing are threatening the health of the oceans and the planet.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.topic: Impact of Oceans on Human Life
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Impact of Oceans on Human Life in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Ocean Pollution and Conservation
text:
Ocean Pollution and Conservation

Key terms: ocean pollution, conservation

The oceans are facing numerous threats, including plastic pollution, overfishing, and climate change. It is essential to take collective action to protect the oceans and preserve them for future generations.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Ocean Pollution and Conservation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Earth's Water Cycle and Oceans
text:
Earth's Water Cycle and Oceans

Key terms: water cycle, ocean role

The Earth's water cycle is essential for life on the planet, and oceans play a crucial role in this process. They help regulate the climate and provide freshwater through precipitation.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Earth's Water Cycle and Oceans in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Oceans and Continents
text:
Oceans and Continents

Key terms: oceans, continents

Oceans are vast water bodies that are interconnected. Continents are large landmasses. There are seven continents in total.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oceans and Continents in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Importance of Oceans
text:
Importance of Oceans

Key terms: marine life, world climate

Oceans support marine life and play a critical role in the world climate. They are affected by human activity and need protection.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Importance of Oceans in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Continents and Oceans
text:
Continents and Oceans

Key terms: continents, oceans, hemispheres

Continents are large landmasses, while oceans are vast water bodies. The Northern Hemisphere has more land than the Southern Hemisphere.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Continents and Oceans in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Definition of Continent
text:
Definition of Continent

Key terms: continent, landmass

A continent is a large landmass. Examples include Asia, Africa, and North America.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Definition of Continent in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Definition of Ocean
text:
Definition of Ocean

Key terms: ocean, water body

An ocean is a vast water body. Examples include the Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, and Indian Ocean.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Definition of Ocean in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Definition of Island
text:
Definition of Island

Key terms: island, landmass

An island is a landmass surrounded by the sea or ocean. Examples include Hawaii and the Maldives.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Definition of Island in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Landforms and Life
text:
Landforms and Life

Key terms: landforms, mountains, plateaus

Landforms are physical features on Earth's surface, shaped over millions of years. They have a significant connection with the environment and life. There are three main types of landforms: mountains, plateaus, and plains.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Landforms and Life in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Types of Mountains
text:
Types of Mountains

Key terms: mountains, highlands, hills

Mountains are landforms with steep slopes and a narrow summit. They can be covered with snow, and their height affects the climate and flora and fauna. There are different types of mountains, including highlands and hills.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Mountains in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Mountain Environment
text:
Mountain Environment

Key terms: mountain environment, terrace farming, waterfalls

Mountain environments are diverse and support a wide range of flora and fauna. The terrain is rugged, and farming is challenging, but terrace farming is practiced in some areas. The mountain environment is also home to many waterfalls and mineral deposits.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Mountain Environment in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Plateaus
text:
Plateaus

Key terms: plateaus, mineral deposits, waterfalls

Plateaus are landforms with a flat surface and steep slopes. They are formed through volcanic activity and are rich in mineral deposits. Plateaus are also home to many waterfalls and have a diverse environment.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Plateaus in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Plains
text:
Plains

Key terms: plains, sediments, agriculture

Plains are landforms with an extensive flat or gently undulating surface. They are formed by rivers depositing sediments, making the soil fertile. Plains are ideal for agriculture and support a variety of flora and fauna.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Plains in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Importance of Landforms
text:
Importance of Landforms

Key terms: landforms, environment, economy

Landforms play a crucial role in shaping the environment and supporting life. They provide habitats for diverse flora and fauna, and their unique features support various economic activities, such as agriculture and mining.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Importance of Landforms in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Challenges of Living in Mountains
text:
Challenges of Living in Mountains

Key terms: mountains, challenges, opportunities

Living in mountains comes with several challenges, including harsh weather conditions, limited access to resources, and potential natural disasters like avalanches and landslides. However, many people choose to live in mountains due to their unique environment and economic opportunities.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Challenges of Living in Mountains in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Landforms and Life
text:
Landforms and Life

Key terms: landforms, adaptability

Humans have adapted to various landforms, including mountains, plateaus, plains, and deserts. Each landform offers unique challenges and opportunities. People's lives and activities have been impacted by the type of landform they live in.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Landforms and Life in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Gangetic Plain
text:
Gangetic Plain

Key terms: Gangetic, plain, fertile

The Gangetic Plain is a fertile region in north India where a large part of the population lives. The main occupations in this region include river fishing and agriculture. The plain is also affected by high population and pollution.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gangetic Plain in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | River Navigation
text:
River Navigation

Key terms: river, navigation, economy

Rivers have supported economic activities, including travel and trade, due to their gentle slope. In the past, people used rivers extensively to travel from one place to another. Today, people still use boats to move around in some areas.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to River Navigation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Deserts
text:
Deserts

Key terms: deserts, dry, unique

Deserts are large and dry expanses with very little precipitation. They have unique flora and fauna. Humans have adapted to most deserts, and communities living in these regions have developed rich cultural traditions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Deserts in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Landform Classification
text:
Landform Classification

Key terms: landforms, classification

Landforms are classified into three main types: mountains, plateaus, and plains. Each landform has distinct physical characteristics and environments. People's lives and activities have been impacted by the type of landform they live in.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Landform Classification in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Resilience
text:
Resilience

Key terms: resilience, adaptability

Resilience is the capacity to meet challenges and difficulties, adapt to them, or overcome them. Humans have demonstrated resilience in various landforms, including deserts. This ability is a testament to human adaptability.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Resilience in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Tiṇais
text:
Tiṇais

Key terms: tiṇais, landscapes

Tiṇais are five landscapes associated with specific deities, lifestyles, moods, or emotions. They reflect a keen awareness of the diverse regions and their characteristics. Tiṇais illustrate the deep connection between humanity and the natural environment.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Tiṇais in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Confluence
text:
Confluence

Key terms: confluence, sacred

A confluence is the meeting point of two or more rivers. Many communities consider a river's source and confluence with one or two other rivers to be sacred. This is reflected in numerous festivals, ceremonies, and rituals conducted at such locations.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Confluence in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What is History?
text:
What is History?

Key terms: history, past, sources

History is the study of the human past. It helps us understand the present by learning from the past. Historians use various sources to reconstruct the past.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is History? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Measuring Time in History
text:
Measuring Time in History

Key terms: time, calendar, BCE, CE

Time is measured in different ways, including the Gregorian calendar, which is used worldwide. The calendar has no 'year zero' and uses BCE (Before Common Era) and CE (Common Era) to mark years.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Measuring Time in History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Timeline in History
text:
Timeline in History

Key terms: timeline, events, order

A timeline is a tool used to mark important events in history. It helps us understand the order in which events took place and how they relate to each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Timeline in History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Sources of History
text:
Sources of History

Key terms: sources, history, objects, texts

Sources of history include objects, structures, texts, and oral traditions. Historians use these sources to reconstruct the past and understand historical events.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sources of History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Early Human History
text:
Early Human History

Key terms: human, history, Homo sapiens

Modern humans (Homo sapiens) have walked the planet for about 300,000 years. Early humans faced many challenges and lived in bands or groups to help each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Early Human History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Human Migration and Settlement
text:
Human Migration and Settlement

Key terms: migration, settlement, technology

Early humans migrated and settled in different parts of the world, adapting to new environments and developing new technologies.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Human Migration and Settlement in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Climate Change and Human History
text:
Climate Change and Human History

Key terms: climate, change, history

The Earth's climate has gone through many changes, affecting human history and migration. The last Ice Age lasted from over 100,000 years ago to around 12,000 years ago.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Climate Change and Human History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Tools and Technology in Human History
text:
Tools and Technology in Human History

Key terms: tools, technology, human

Early humans developed tools and technologies that made their lives easier, such as improved stone axes and blades, arrowheads, and fire.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.topic: Tools and Technology in Human History
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Tools and Technology in Human History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Ice Ages
text:
Ice Ages

Key terms: Ice Age, climate, Earth

The Earth's climate has gone through many changes, including Ice Ages where much of the planet was covered in ice. This happened several times, with the last Ice Age lasting from over 100,000 years ago to around 12,000 years ago. The climate warmed up afterwards, and humans started settling down and cultivating crops.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ice Ages in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Early Human Settlements
text:
Early Human Settlements

Key terms: settlements, fertile soil, complex societies

As the climate warmed up, humans started settling down near rivers and cultivating crops. They domesticated animals and grew in size and number, often settling near fertile soil. This was a significant change in human history, marking the beginning of more complex societies.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Early Human Settlements in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Social Complexity
text:
Social Complexity

Key terms: social complexity, chieftains, collective ownership

As communities grew, their social complexity increased. Leaders or 'chieftains' emerged to ensure the well-being of the people, and everyone worked together for the community's welfare. There was no sense of individual ownership, and lands were collectively sowed and harvested.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Social Complexity in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Timeline and Sources of History
text:
Timeline and Sources of History

Key terms: timeline, sources of history, interpretation

A timeline helps us understand the sequence of historical events at different times. There are different ways of measuring time, and sources of history help us reconstruct and interpret past events. By studying these, we can learn more about our past and the people who came before us.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Timeline and Sources of History in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Welfare and Prosperity
text:
Welfare and Prosperity

Key terms: welfare, prosperity, collective approach

Welfare refers to the overall health, prosperity, and well-being of a community. In early human societies, people worked together to ensure the community's welfare, and there was no sense of individual ownership. This collective approach helped them thrive and grow.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Welfare and Prosperity in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Hamlets and Villages
text:
Hamlets and Villages

Key terms: hamlets, villages, networks of communication

A hamlet is a small settlement or village, and as communities grew, they developed into sizeable villages that exchanged goods. These villages eventually grew into small towns, and networks of communication and exchange were established.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Hamlets and Villages in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Emergence of Civilisation
text:
Emergence of Civilisation

Key terms: civilisation, technologies, complex societies

The early progress of humanity laid the groundwork for the emergence of civilisation. This involved the development of new technologies, such as pottery and metalworking, and the growth of complex societies. Civilisation marked a significant turning point in human history.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Emergence of Civilisation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Defining India
text:
Defining India

Key terms: India, Bhārata, Jambudvīpa

India is a country with a rich history and diverse geography. It has been known by many names over the centuries, including 'Bhārata' and 'Jambudvīpa'. The country's name has evolved over time, reflecting its cultural and geographical identity.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Defining India in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Ancient Names for India
text:
Ancient Names for India

Key terms: Sapta Sindhava, Bhārata, Indus River

The ancient inhabitants of India gave the country various names, such as 'Sapta Sindhava' and 'Bhārata'. These names were often derived from geographical features, like the Indus River. The names reflect the cultural and geographical identity of the region.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ancient Names for India in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Foreign Names for India
text:
Foreign Names for India

Key terms: Hind, Hidu, Hindu

Foreign visitors and invaders of India gave the country various names, such as 'Hind', 'Hidu', and 'Hindu'. These names were often derived from the Indus River or other geographical features. The names reflect the cultural and geographical identity of the region.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Foreign Names for India in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Evolution of India's Name
text:
Evolution of India's Name

Key terms: Bhārata, Hindustān, India

The name of India has evolved over time, reflecting its cultural and geographical identity. The country was known as 'Bhārata' in ancient times, and later as 'Hindustān'. The name 'India' was adopted from the Persian word 'Hindu'.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Evolution of India's Name in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Geographical Boundaries of India
text:
Geographical Boundaries of India

Key terms: Bhārata, Hindustān, India

The geographical boundaries of India have changed over time, reflecting its cultural and geographical identity. The country was known as 'Bhārata' in ancient times, and later as 'Hindustān'. The name 'India' was adopted from the Persian word 'Hindu'.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Geographical Boundaries of India in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Cultural Significance of India's Name
text:
Cultural Significance of India's Name

Key terms: cultural significance, India's name, cultural heritage

The name of India has cultural significance, reflecting its rich history and diverse geography. The country's name has evolved over time, reflecting its cultural and geographical identity. The name 'India' is a symbol of the country's cultural heritage.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Cultural Significance of India's Name in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What is a Civilisation?
text:
What is a Civilisation?

Key terms: civilisation, society

A civilisation is an advanced stage of human societies with characteristics such as government, urbanism, crafts, trade, writing, cultural ideas, and productive agriculture. It's a complex society with many activities that need to be managed.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What is a Civilisation? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Characteristics of a Civilisation
text:
Characteristics of a Civilisation

Key terms: characteristics, civilisation

A civilisation should have at least 7 characteristics: government, urbanism, crafts, trade, writing, cultural ideas, and productive agriculture. These characteristics are essential for the development of a complex society.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Characteristics of a Civilisation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Civilisation
text:
Harappan Civilisation

Key terms: Harappan, civilisation

The Harappan civilisation was one of the oldest civilisations in the world, located in the Indus Valley region. It was a well-balanced community with a strong emphasis on water management, cleanliness, and trade.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Civilisation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Water Management in Harappan Cities
text:
Water Management in Harappan Cities

Key terms: water, management

The Harappans gave much importance to water management and cleanliness. They built separate areas for bathing, connected to a larger network of drains, and had individual bathrooms in their homes.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Water Management in Harappan Cities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Agriculture
text:
Harappan Agriculture

Key terms: agriculture, Harappan

The Harappans grew cereals like barley, wheat, and rice, as well as pulses and vegetables. They also domesticated animals for meat consumption and fished in rivers and the sea.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Agriculture in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Trade
text:
Harappan Trade

Key terms: trade, Harappan

The Harappans were engaged in active trade, both within their own civilisation and with other civilisations and cultures. They exported ornaments, timber, and other goods, and imported copper and other materials.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Trade in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | The Indus-Sarasvatī Civilisation
text:
The Indus-Sarasvatī Civilisation

Key terms: Indus-Sarasvatī, civilisation

The Indus-Sarasvatī civilisation was a major civilisation in the Indian subcontinent, known for its advanced urban planning, water management, and trade. It was one of the oldest civilisations in the world.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to The Indus-Sarasvatī Civilisation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | The Significance of the Harappan Civilisation
text:
The Significance of the Harappan Civilisation

Key terms: significance, Harappan

The Harappan civilisation was a significant milestone in human history, demonstrating advanced urban planning, water management, and trade. It laid the foundation for the development of future civilisations.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.topic: The Significance of the Harappan Civilisation
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to The Significance of the Harappan Civilisation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Crafts
text:
Harappan Crafts

Key terms: Harappan, crafts, techniques

Harappans developed special techniques to drill and decorate beads, conch shells, and other materials. They used these techniques to create beautiful crafts, such as shell bangles and intricate designs. This shows their skill and creativity as craftsmen.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Crafts in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Trade
text:
Harappan Trade

Key terms: Harappan, trade, maritime

The Harappans traded goods with other civilizations, using land routes, rivers, and the sea. They imported copper and other valuable materials, and exported goods such as beads and shell bangles. This trade helped to establish their civilization as a major player in the region.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Trade in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Seals
text:
Harappan Seals

Key terms: Harappan, seals, symbols

The Harappans used small seals to identify their goods and themselves. These seals were made of steatite and featured animal figures and writing signs. Although the meaning of these symbols is still unclear, they likely played a role in trade and communication.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Harappan Seals in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Daily Life
text:
Harappan Daily Life

Key terms: Harappan, daily life, crafts

The Harappans lived in planned cities with efficient water management and diverse crafts. They used bronze and other materials to create tools, pots, and pans, and designed games and toys to keep themselves entertained. This shows their ability to adapt to their environment and create a comfortable life.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Harappan Daily Life in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Decline
text:
Harappan Decline

Key terms: Harappan, decline, environmental

The Harappan civilization declined around 1900 BCE, likely due to climatic and environmental changes. The cities were abandoned, and the people returned to a rural lifestyle. This shows how the civilization was affected by external factors and how it adapted to change.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Harappan Decline in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Legacy
text:
Harappan Legacy

Key terms: Harappan, legacy, culture

Although the Harappan civilization declined, its legacy lived on. The people passed on their culture and technology to the next phase of Indian civilization. This shows how the Harappans contributed to the development of Indian society and culture.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Harappan Legacy in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Water Management
text:
Harappan Water Management

Key terms: Harappan, water management, reservoirs

The Harappans developed a sophisticated system of reservoirs and wells to manage water. This allowed them to conserve water and maintain a stable supply, which was essential for their civilization. This shows their ability to adapt to their environment and create innovative solutions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Harappan Water Management in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Harappan Civic Sense
text:
Harappan Civic Sense

Key terms: Harappan, civic sense, community

The Harappans had a high civic sense, as shown by their well-planned cities and efficient water management. They also maintained public wells and other infrastructure, which suggests a strong sense of community and responsibility. This shows how the Harappans valued their community and worked together to create a better life.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Harappan Civic Sense in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | What are the Vedas?
text:
What are the Vedas?

Key terms: Vedas, hymns, prayers

The Vedas are ancient Indian texts that contain thousands of hymns and prayers. They were composed orally and passed down through generations. The four main Vedas are the Ṛig Veda, the Yajur Veda, the Sāma Veda, and the Atharva Veda.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to What are the Vedas? in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Vedic Society
text:
Vedic Society

Key terms: clans, jana, assembly

Vedic society was organized into different clans or janas. Each clan was associated with a particular region of the northwest part of the Subcontinent. The Vedas mention various professions and a collective gathering or assembly.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Vedic Society in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Vedic Schools of Thought
text:
Vedic Schools of Thought

Key terms: Upaniṣhads, Vedanta, brahman

Vedic culture developed many rituals and texts, including the Upaniṣhads, which introduced new concepts like rebirth and karma. The Vedanta school of thought believed that everything is one divine essence called brahman.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Vedic Schools of Thought in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | The Buddha
text:
The Buddha

Key terms: Buddha, enlightenment, ahimsa

Siddhārtha Gautama was a young prince who became the Buddha after achieving enlightenment. He taught the idea of ahimsa, or non-hurting, and the importance of inner discipline.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to The Buddha in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Jainism
text:
Jainism

Key terms: Jainism, ahimsa, anekāntavāda

Jainism is a school of thought that emerged around the same time as Buddhism. It teaches the importance of ahimsa, anekāntavāda, and aparigraha, and emphasizes the conquest of ignorance and attachments.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Jainism in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Spirituality
text:
Spirituality

Key terms: spirituality, reality, truth

Spirituality is the search for a deeper or higher dimension beyond our current personality. It involves seeking the truths of this world and understanding the nature of reality.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Spirituality in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Consciousness
text:
Consciousness

Key terms: consciousness, awareness, self

Consciousness is the quality or state of being aware of something within oneself. It is an important concept in many Indian philosophical traditions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Consciousness in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Attachment
text:
Attachment

Key terms: attachment, bond, habit

Attachment is the condition of having a bond with someone or something, usually through sentiment or habit. It is an important concept in many Indian philosophical traditions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Attachment in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Jainism's Main Teachings
text:
Jainism's Main Teachings

Key terms: ahimsa, anekāntavāda, aparigraha

Jainism teaches ahimsa (non-violence), anekāntavāda (many perspectives), and aparigraha (non-attachment). These ideas help individuals understand the interconnectedness of all living beings and strive for enlightenment.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Jainism's Main Teachings in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Buddhist Values
text:
Buddhist Values

Key terms: right action, right thinking, selflessness

Buddhism emphasizes the importance of right action and right thinking. The Jātaka tales illustrate Buddhist values such as selflessness and compassion. These stories teach individuals to live a virtuous life and strive for enlightenment.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Buddhist Values in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Tribal Belief Systems
text:
Tribal Belief Systems

Key terms: tribal, sacred land, divinity

Tribal belief systems in India are diverse and complex. They often regard the land and its features as sacred and have a higher concept of divinity. Tribal art and practices have interacted with Hinduism for centuries, resulting in mutual enrichment.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Tribal Belief Systems in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Vedic Schools of Thought
text:
Vedic Schools of Thought

Key terms: Vedanta, Yoga, dharma

The Vedas gave rise to several schools of thought, including Vedanta and Yoga. These schools emphasized the importance of dharma, karma, and rebirth. They also shared common concepts such as the search for an end to suffering and ignorance.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Vedic Schools of Thought in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Interconnectedness of All Living Beings
text:
Interconnectedness of All Living Beings

Key terms: interconnectedness, ahimsa, compassion

Jainism and Buddhism emphasize the interconnectedness of all living beings. This concept is reflected in the idea of ahimsa (non-violence) and the importance of treating all living beings with compassion and respect.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Interconnectedness of All Living Beings in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Indian Cultural Roots
text:
Indian Cultural Roots

Key terms: Indian culture, banyan tree, unity

Indian culture has a rich and diverse heritage, influenced by various schools of thought, folk traditions, and tribal belief systems. The banyan tree is a symbol of Indian civilization, representing its deep roots, unity, and diversity.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Indian Cultural Roots in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Concept of Higher Divinity
text:
Concept of Higher Divinity

Key terms: higher divinity, supreme being, natural elements

Many tribal groups in India have a concept of a higher divinity or supreme being. This concept is reflected in the worship of deities associated with natural elements and the recognition of a higher power beyond human understanding.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Concept of Higher Divinity in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Importance of Right Thinking
text:
Importance of Right Thinking

Key terms: right thinking, positive thoughts, negative thoughts

Buddhism emphasizes the importance of right thinking, which involves cultivating positive thoughts and avoiding negative ones. This concept is reflected in the Jātaka tales and the teachings of the Buddha.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Importance of Right Thinking in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Unity in Diversity
text:
Unity in Diversity

Key terms: unity, diversity, India

Unity in diversity is a concept where different elements come together to form a whole. In India, this concept is seen in its diverse cultures, languages, and traditions that are united under a single identity. This concept is not unique to India and can be seen in other cultures as well.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Unity in Diversity in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Indian Diversity
text:
Indian Diversity

Key terms: diversity, India, culture

India is a country with immense diversity in its landscapes, people, languages, dresses, foods, festivals, and customs. This diversity is not limited to one region but is spread across the country. India's diversity is a result of its long history, geographical location, and cultural influences.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Indian Diversity in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Common Food Grains
text:
Common Food Grains

Key terms: food, grains, India

In India, there are certain food grains that are common to almost every part of the country. These include cereals such as rice, barley, and wheat, and millets such as pearl millet, sorghum, and finger millet. These grains are the staple food for most Indians.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Common Food Grains in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Sari as a Unifying Factor
text:
Sari as a Unifying Factor

Key terms: sari, unity, culture

The sari is a traditional Indian dress that is worn in most parts of the country. Despite its diverse designs, fabrics, and colors, the sari is a unifying factor in Indian culture. It is a symbol of Indian tradition and is worn on various occasions.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sari as a Unifying Factor in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Festivals in India
text:
Festivals in India

Key terms: festivals, India, culture

India has a rich cultural heritage and celebrates a variety of festivals throughout the year. These festivals are not limited to one region but are celebrated across the country. Some of the common festivals celebrated in India include Makara Sankranti, Pongal, and Diwali.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Festivals in India in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Indian Epics
text:
Indian Epics

Key terms: epics, India, culture

The Rāmāyaṇa and the Mahābhārata are two ancient Indian epics that have been translated or adapted into regional languages. These epics have been a part of Indian culture for centuries and have been transmitted orally through generations. They contain stories of heroes who fought to re-establish dharma.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Indian Epics in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Unity in Diversity in Indian Culture
text:
Unity in Diversity in Indian Culture

Key terms: unity, diversity, culture

Indian culture celebrates diversity as an enrichment, but never loses sight of the underlying unity that nourishes that diversity. This concept is seen in the country's diverse cultures, languages, and traditions that are united under a single identity.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.topic: Unity in Diversity in Indian Culture
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Unity in Diversity in Indian Culture in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Family Importance
text:
Family Importance

Key terms: family, society, roles

The family is the fundamental unit of society. It provides love, care, and support to its members. Family members work together and have roles and responsibilities towards each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Family Importance in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Types of Families
text:
Types of Families

Key terms: joint, nuclear, families

There are two main types of families: joint families and nuclear families. Joint families have multiple generations living together, while nuclear families consist of a couple and their children.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Families in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Family Roles and Responsibilities
text:
Family Roles and Responsibilities

Key terms: roles, responsibilities, family

Each family member has a role and responsibility towards others. Parents are responsible for raising their children, while children help with household chores and take on more responsibilities as they grow up.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Family Roles and Responsibilities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Community Definition
text:
Community Definition

Key terms: community, group, support

A community is a group of people connected by shared interests, work, or location. Members of a community work together and support each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Community Definition in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Types of Communities
text:
Types of Communities

Key terms: types, communities, shared

There are various types of communities, including residential communities, communities based on shared interests, and communities based on shared work or location.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Communities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Interdependence of Communities
text:
Interdependence of Communities

Key terms: interdependence, communities, resources

Communities are interdependent, meaning they rely on each other for support and resources. This is evident in the way communities work together to achieve common goals.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Interdependence of Communities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Community Support
text:
Community Support

Key terms: community, support, essential

Community support is essential for individuals and families. It can take many forms, including financial, emotional, and practical support.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Community Support in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Rules and Regulations in Communities
text:
Rules and Regulations in Communities

Key terms: rules, regulations, communities

Communities often have rules and regulations to maintain order and ensure the well-being of its members. These rules can be formal or informal and may vary depending on the community.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Rules and Regulations in Communities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Governance
text:
Governance

Key terms: governance, government

Governance is the process of taking decisions, organizing society's life with different sets of rules, and ensuring they are followed. The group of individuals or system that makes the rules and ensures they are followed is called a government.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Governance in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Democracy
text:
Democracy

Key terms: democracy, people, power

Democracy is a system where the people have the power to make decisions. It is a system where citizens can participate in the decision-making process and have a say in the laws that govern them.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Democracy in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Three Organs of Government
text:
Three Organs of Government

Key terms: legislature, executive, judiciary

The three organs of government are the legislature, executive, and judiciary. The legislature makes laws, the executive implements laws, and the judiciary interprets laws.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Three Organs of Government in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Separation of Powers
text:
Separation of Powers

Key terms: separation, powers, balance

The separation of powers is a system where the three organs of government are kept separate, but work together. This ensures that each organ can check the other and maintain balance.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Separation of Powers in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Levels of Government
text:
Levels of Government

Key terms: levels, government, responsibilities

Governments operate at different levels, including local, state, and national. Each level deals with different matters and has its own set of responsibilities.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Levels of Government in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Representative Democracy
text:
Representative Democracy

Key terms: representative, democracy, assembly

In a representative democracy, citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf. These representatives discuss laws and problems in assemblies and try to convince each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Representative Democracy in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Grassroots Democracy
text:
Grassroots Democracy

Key terms: grassroots, democracy, participation

Grassroots democracy is a system that enables and encourages the participation of ordinary citizens in decision-making. Citizens can have a say in decisions that affect them.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Grassroots Democracy in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Governance and Government
text:
Governance and Government

Key terms: governance, government, legislative

No country can function without a system of governance and government. A government has three main parts: legislative, executive, and judiciary, which work together. These parts help make and enforce laws, and ensure the country runs smoothly.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Governance and Government in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Three Organs of Government
text:
Three Organs of Government

Key terms: legislative, executive, judiciary

A modern government has three organs: legislative, executive, and judiciary. These organs need to work together to make the government function properly. Each organ has its own role and responsibilities.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Three Organs of Government in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Levels of Government
text:
Levels of Government

Key terms: national, state, local

The Indian government functions at three levels: Centre or national, State, and local. This means that there are different levels of government that work together to manage the country. Each level has its own powers and responsibilities.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Levels of Government in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Democracy Framework
text:
Democracy Framework

Key terms: democracy, elected, representatives

Democracy is the overall framework for the system of government in India. It functions through elected representatives, both at the State and national levels. This means that citizens elect their representatives to make decisions on their behalf.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Democracy Framework in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Grassroots Democracy
text:
Grassroots Democracy

Key terms: democracy, local, participation

Grassroots democracy is a system where people participate directly in decision-making processes at the local level. It brings governance closer to the people, making it possible for them to actively participate in decision-making processes.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Grassroots Democracy in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Panchayati Raj System
text:
Panchayati Raj System

Key terms: panchayat, self-government, local

Panchayati Raj is a form of self-government where village councils, called Panchayats, play a vital role in addressing local issues, promoting development, and ensuring that the benefits of government schemes reach the grassroots level.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Panchayati Raj System in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Three-Tier System
text:
Three-Tier System

Key terms: tier, system, levels

The Panchayati Raj system works at three levels: village, block, and district. Each level has its own set of responsibilities and functions, working together to cover almost all aspects of life in the district.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Three-Tier System in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Gram Panchayat
text:
Gram Panchayat

Key terms: gram, panchayat, village

A Gram Panchayat is a village council that is closest to the people in rural areas. Its members are elected directly by the Gram Sabha, and it plays a vital role in addressing local issues and promoting development.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gram Panchayat in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Sarpanch
text:
Sarpanch

Key terms: sarpanch, head, president

A Sarpanch is the head or president of a Gram Panchayat. They are elected by the Gram Sabha and play a key role in decision-making processes and implementing development projects.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sarpanch in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Panchayat Samiti
text:
Panchayat Samiti

Key terms: panchayat, samiti, block

A Panchayat Samiti is an institution that exists at the block level and is responsible for coordinating matters across Gram Panchayats. It plays a vital role in strengthening the participation of local people and facilitating the allotment of funds for development projects.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Panchayat Samiti in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Disadvantaged Sections
text:
Disadvantaged Sections

Key terms: disadvantaged, sections, society

Disadvantaged sections of society include people who are marginalized, oppressed, or have limited access to resources and opportunities. The government has made special rules to ensure that their needs and problems are heard and addressed.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Disadvantaged Sections in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Child-Friendly Panchayat
text:
Child-Friendly Panchayat

Key terms: child-friendly, panchayat, children

A child-friendly panchayat is a Gram Panchayat that actively involves children in decision-making processes and addresses their needs and concerns. It plays a vital role in promoting child development and well-being.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Child-Friendly Panchayat in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Urban Local Bodies
text:
Urban Local Bodies

Key terms: Urban, Local, Bodies

Urban local bodies are decentralised structures in urban areas that manage various functions affecting citizens' lives. They are responsible for infrastructure, waste management, and economic development. These bodies have elected members who represent local citizens.

metadata.subject: Social Science

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Decentralised Governance
text:
Decentralised Governance

Key terms: Decentralised, Governance

Decentralised governance in urban areas works through different urban local bodies that perform various functions. This system allows citizens to participate in decision-making and have a direct say in how their areas are managed.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Decentralised Governance in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Elected Members
text:
Elected Members

Elected members in urban local bodies represent local citizens and make decisions on their behalf. These members are responsible for ensuring that the local bodies perform their functions efficiently.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Citizen Duties
text:
Citizen Duties

Citizens have duties to ensure that urban local bodies perform their functions efficiently. This includes participating in decision-making, reporting problems, and following instructions regarding waste segregation.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Citizen Duties in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Urban Governance System
text:
Urban Governance System

Key terms: Urban, Governance, System

The urban governance system is more complex and diverse than the rural system. It requires a more complex system to manage various functions and ensure efficient performance.

metadata.subject: Social Science

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Participatory Democracy
text:
Participatory Democracy

Participatory democracy is a broader concept that aims to empower citizens to actively participate in their country's functioning. It involves decentralised governance and decision-making at various levels.

text:
Urban Local Body Functions

Urban local bodies are responsible for various functions such as infrastructure management, waste management, and economic development. They also have a role in planning for the area's economic and social development.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Similarities and Differences
text:
Similarities and Differences

The Panchayati Raj system in rural areas and urban local bodies have similarities and differences. Both systems involve decentralised governance and decision-making, but the urban system is more complex and diverse.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Types of Economic Activities
text:
Types of Economic Activities

Key terms: Economic, Non-Economic, Activities

Economic activities are divided into two groups: economic activities and non-economic activities. Economic activities involve money or are performed in exchange for money, while non-economic activities do not generate income but are done out of feelings like gratitude, love, care, and respect.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Types of Economic Activities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Value Addition
text:
Value Addition

Key terms: Value, Addition, Economic

Value addition is the process of transforming something into another form, adding value at each stage. This is seen in economic activities where goods or services are created and sold, generating income.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Value Addition in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Payment in Kind
text:
Payment in Kind

Payment in kind is a non-cash payment received for work performed, where the payment is in the form of goods or services rather than money.

text:
Importance of Non-Economic Activities

Non-economic activities contribute to social welfare, personal wellbeing, and enhance the overall quality of life, even though they may not generate income.

Value of Community Participation

Community participation in activities like cleaning, tree plantation, and festivals brings people together and contributes to social welfare and personal wellbeing.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Value of Community Participation in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Compensation for Economic Activities
text:
Compensation for Economic Activities

People are compensated for economic activities in various ways, including salary, wages, payment in kind, and fees.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Compensation for Economic Activities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Economic Activities
text:
Economic Activities

Key terms: Economic Activities, Primary Sector, Secondary Sector, Tertiary Sector

Economic activities are activities that create monetary value. They are classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors. The primary sector involves extracting raw materials from nature, the secondary sector involves processing these raw materials into products, and the tertiary sector involves providing services that support both primary and secondary sectors.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Economic Activities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Primary Sector
text:
Primary Sector

Key terms: Primary Sector, Raw Materials, Nature

The primary sector involves extracting raw materials from nature, such as farming, mining, and forestry. These activities are directly dependent on nature and provide the basic inputs for other sectors.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Primary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Secondary Sector
text:
Secondary Sector

Key terms: Secondary Sector, Processing, Manufacturing

The secondary sector involves processing raw materials into products, such as manufacturing, construction, and utilities. These activities transform raw materials into goods and services that can be sold or consumed.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Secondary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Tertiary Sector
text:
Tertiary Sector

Key terms: Tertiary Sector, Services, Support

The tertiary sector involves providing services that support both primary and secondary sectors, such as transportation, banking, and communication. These services enable the smooth functioning of other sectors and provide value to consumers.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Tertiary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Interdependence Among Sectors
text:
Interdependence Among Sectors

Key terms: Interdependence, Sectors, Dependence

The three sectors are interconnected and dependent on each other. The primary sector provides raw materials for the secondary sector, which processes them into products. The tertiary sector provides services that support both primary and secondary sectors.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Interdependence Among Sectors in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Classification of Economic Activities
text:
Classification of Economic Activities

Key terms: Classification, Economic Activities, Sectors

Economic activities can be classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors based on their characteristics and functions. This classification helps us understand how economic activities function and the links they have with each other.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Classification of Economic Activities in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Importance of Economic Activities
text:
Importance of Economic Activities

Economic activities are essential for the prosperity of a nation. They provide goods and services that meet the needs of people and contribute to the country's growth and development.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Importance of Economic Activities in Grade 6 Social Science.

text:
Examples of Economic Activities

Examples of economic activities include farming, mining, manufacturing, transportation, and communication. These activities are essential for the functioning of the economy and provide goods and services that meet the needs of people.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Primary Sector
text:
Primary Sector

Key terms: primary, sector, raw, materials

The primary sector involves activities like farming, fishing, and mining. These activities are related to the production of raw materials. For example, a farmer grows wheat, a fisherman catches fish, and a miner extracts coal.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Primary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Secondary Sector
text:
Secondary Sector

Key terms: secondary, sector, manufacturing, processing

The secondary sector involves activities like manufacturing and processing. These activities take raw materials from the primary sector and turn them into goods. For example, a factory takes wheat from a farmer and turns it into bread.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Secondary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Tertiary Sector
text:
Tertiary Sector

Key terms: tertiary, sector, services, sale

The tertiary sector involves activities like providing services. These activities are related to the sale of goods and services. For example, a shopkeeper sells bread to customers, and a teacher provides education services.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Tertiary Sector in Grade 6 Social Science.

title: NCERT Grade 6 Social Science | Interdependence
text:
Interdependence

Key terms: interdependence, sectors, rely, function

The primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors are interdependent. This means that they rely on each other to function. For example, a farmer needs a factory to process his wheat, and a factory needs a shopkeeper to sell its products.

metadata.subject: Social Science
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Interdependence in Grade 6 Social Science.
